unmapped_findings: Measured chemical composition of the 15Mn5Ni alloy (Table 1, wt.%, balance Fe): Mn 14.7 ± 0.3, Al 9.8 ± 0.05, C 0.9 ± 0.01, Ni 4.1 ± 0.05.

The 15Mn5Ni alloy in the HR condition contained a higher B2 fraction (~12%) than 28Mn5Ni (~4%), and the alloy composition series was designed to give a B2 fraction varying from 0 to ~12% in the hot-rolled condition.

In the HR condition the three LDS alloys exhibited about 20–70% total tensile elongation to failure at room temperature (from prior study [21]), with the 15Mn5Ni alloy displaying the lowest ductility; this suggested an increased tendency for cracking when cold rolling exceeds 50% reduction.
The 15Mn5Ni alloy experienced cracking beyond 50% cold reduction; hence cold rolling was restricted to ~50% reduction for all alloys for comparison.

The hot-rolled microstructures of all three alloys (including 15Mn5Ni) were reported in a previous study [21] and serve as the starting condition for the cold rolling study; the present paper's detailed EBSD/XRD/TEM characterization focuses on the HR+CR and heat-treated conditions.
